title: Paradise Lost
author: John Milton
teaches: the rebel angel's argument, which is sophisticated and loses -- and the losing is the point
fruit: Satan's address to the fallen host is the most persuasive piece of rhetoric in English arguing that the self-interested course is the right one. He is right about everything except the one thing, and the poem's whole weight is on that exception.

title: The Tragical History of Doctor Faustus
author: Christopher Marlowe
teaches: the same bargain as Goethe's Faust, earlier and colder -- and the difference in what the devil asks for
fruit: the cost is not given at the start, it is taken in instalments: Faustus gives up one thing at a time and believes each piece is a gain. The play's twenty-four years are the instalment plan.

title: The White Devil
author: John Webster
teaches: every social advantage the infernal one lacks: the most successful devil of the Renaissance stage
fruit: the White Devil is the one who does not need a disguise and does not need a prohibition. He is the adversary who wins on his own terms, which is the case a gate keyed on suspicion will not catch.

title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
author: George Orwell
teaches: the Newspeak appendix -- a language designed so that a thought cannot be had: a lie that cannot be stated even by itself
fruit: the appendix is the densest statement of the whole project: a vocabulary whose second principle is that nothing exists that cannot be said, and a second principle that makes the first one true.
